steps.note: BleepingComputer reports Kroll saw activity in April 2022 and as early as July 2021 pulling back org info; Mandiant ties the May 19-22 RDP certs to second-stage hosts, not the scanning hosts, but reported fits.
Progress describes the unauthenticated SQLi DB access, CISA says CL0P exploited it from May 27 per open-source info and added it to KEV on June 2.
CISA calls LEMURLOOT a C# web shell used for persistence and data theft, and Mandiant notes theft within minutes of deployment.
Mandiant says human2.aspx masquerades as human.aspx, requires a GUID header and returns 404 otherwise.
Mandiant lists enumerating files and folders and retrieving configuration, and CISA lists enumerating the SQL database.
Mandiant and CISA describe creating and deleting a Health Check Service admin user, and CISA warns the accounts survive a web server rebuild.
CISA and Mandiant confirm the shell reads Azure Blob settings and keys, Progress advises rotating keys, and the conservative reported label fits the unconfirmed Azure theft.
Mandiant reports large gzip-compressed file theft from different hosts than the exploit, and CISA says the shell stole data from MOVEit databases.
Talos gives a June 5 leak-site post with a June 14 deadline, Mandiant gives June 6 and FIN11, and BleepingComputer cites Microsoft's Lace Tempest link.

covered.note: Matches output exploit-sql-injection, attacker to MOVEit web app via unauthenticated SQLi.
No output step describes turning SQLi database access into admin-level control of the app.
No output step describes the app being made to run attacker code on the Windows server.
Matches output plant-web-shell, with the human2.aspx detail in disguise-web-shell.
Matches output create-admin-account, web shell adding a Health Check Service admin to the database.
Matches output map-files-and-database, web shell listing the database, files and folders.
Matches output grab-azure-keys, web shell reading Azure Blob settings and keys.
Matches output steal-files, bulk compressed file download from MOVEit to the attacker.
Matches output extort-victims, CL0P pressing victims through its leak site.
